name: BY ANY OTHER NAME
clue: Renamed for Constantine in 330 A.D., the city astride the Bosporus has officially gone by this name only since 1930

name: MATH IMMORTALS
clue: This prolific Swiss mathematician's famous identity unites e, i, pi, 1 and 0 in a single equation

name: NOBEL PHYSICS

name: DYSTOPIAN TITLES
clue: Ray Bradbury titled this novel after the temperature at which he was told book paper catches fire

name: UNFINISHED BUSINESS

name: ONE-BOOK WONDER

name: HIGH FIVES

name: CROWNING MOMENTS

name: POETRY IN MOTION
clue: Baltimore's NFL team takes its name from an 1845 poem by this writer, who died in that city and was buried there in 1849

name: CHAIN REACTIONS

name: COLD WAR CHESS

name: FOLK HEROES

name: FULL CIRCLE

name: ALOHA MEANS GOODBYE

name: PLANETARY NAMES

name: QUIET ON THE SET

name: CAPITAL NAMESAKES

name: MEDICAL IMMORTALITY

name: ELEMENT OF SURPRISE

name: SHOT IN THE ARM

name: DRAWN TO GREATNESS

name: EUROPEAN RIVERS

name: CURRENT AFFAIRS

name: MEMORY LANE

name: FOILED AGAIN!

name: WORLD WAR II
clue: Clouds over the primary target of Kokura diverted the second atomic bomb to this city in August 1945

name: HOMESICK HARMONIES
clue: Homesick for Bohemia while directing a New York conservatory, he wrote his Symphony No. 9, 'From the New World,' in 1893

name: DAYS OF THE WEEK
clue: Thursday belongs to the thunder god Thor, and this day of the week honors his one-eyed father

name: WORLD CUP HISTORY
clue: In 1930 this nation of some 2 million people hosted the first FIFA World Cup and won it too

name: PERFECT SEASONS
clue: The 1972 edition of this AFC team capped the NFL's first perfect 17-0 season by beating Washington in Super Bowl VII
